Please provide an MRP to make this easier to test and fix:
- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue, with no unnecessary files included. Be sure to not include the `.godot` folder in the archive (but keep `project.godot`).
- Having an MRP is very important for contributors to be able to reproduce the bug in the same way that you are experiencing it. When testing a potential fix for the issue, contributors will use the MRP to validate that the fix is working as intended.
- Drag and drop a ZIP archive to upload it (max 10 MB). **Do not select another field until the project is done uploading.**
- **Note for C# users:** If your issue is *not* C#-specific, please upload a minimal reproduction project written in GDScript. This will make it easier for contributors to reproduce the issue locally as not everyone has a .NET setup available.

Sure, here you go. After facing a problem where I couldn't get the error on the MRP, I found out that enabling `physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread` was the reason for this error.
[issue_project_109213_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21561838/issue_project_109213_mrp.zip)

This should indeed be fixed, but a workaround is to move the two variable definitions

```
var shape = SphereShape3D.new()
var params = PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D.new()
```

out of the `sphere_trace` function, to the top of the script as member variables.

(This also reduces the number of memory allocations.)

That's a great news ! 
Yes after reading back my code later I found a lot of things I could have optimized 😅, thanks for the tip.

This issue is indeed due to how `physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread` works.

The problem is that the creation of the query collision shape happens asynchronously, whereas the query itself happens immediately, which effectively leads to a race condition.

With Jolt this race condition presents itself as this error, as the query shape doesn't really exist until the first `PhysicsServer3D.shape_set_data` call (which happens under the hood when you create your `SphereShape3D`) is processed/flushed by the physics server, after the physics processing is done.

With Godot Physics (both 2D and 3D), this race condition instead presented itself as the query sometimes (subject to the random nature of multi-threading) failing to hit anything, due to `shape_set_data` sometimes not being flushed before the `collide_shape` call.

So this is essentially another manifestation of #109554, which also means that #109591 changed the behavior in a significant way, as the flushing of this `shape_set_data` call will now never[^1] happen in time for the `collide_shape` call, meaning you will always see this error when using Jolt, and you will never hit anything when using Godot Physics.

The only real "solution" to this (without serious refactoring) would be to change all physics queries to always flush the entire `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT` command queue before running, so as to ensure the most up-to-date physics data, essentially treating queries the same as any other `PhysicsServer*DWrapMT` getter. However, given the prevalence of physics queries in most games, as well as `physics/common/enable_object_picking` being enabled by default, this would likely be quite detrimental to performance for anyone relying on `physics/*d/run_on_separate_thread`.

You can technically force this flushing yourself by calling something like `PhysicsServer3D.shape_get_data(shape)` (and just discard the return value) right after creating your `SphereShape3D`, thus "fixing" the problem in much the same way, but the suggestion by @rburing to create the query shape earlier (with the correct radius) is preferrable. Note however that creating the `SphereShape3D` beforehand and then changing its radius (or any other shape data) right before the query would not work, as the query will then just use stale shape data instead.

I suspect we'll see more of these reports come in once 4.5-stable is released, now that #109554 has made this race condition more obvious, for both 2D and 3D physics.

[^1]: Unless you manage to force a flush of the physics server command buffer.
